title: cuscuta planiflora var. madagascariensis
intro: Cuscuta planiflora var. madagascariensis, commonly known as Dodder, is a parasitic plant that obtains its nutrients by connecting itself to the vascular tissue of another plant. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues, due to its health benefits such as anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Cuscuta planiflora var. madagascariensis include its ability to reduce fever, relieve pain, and improve digestion, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents including flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids. However, further research is required to fully understand the extent of its health benefits and potential side effects.
